transcript: Today my boyfriend Paul and I went to see White Girl in danger, a new musical by Michael R. Jackson, the writer of A Strange Loop. The show is kind of hard to explain, but act one is largely a satire on white girl problems commonly seen in modern sitcoms, and hilariously critiques the way black people are often sidelined as background characters. Act 2 has more explicit commentary on black representation and how black characters shouldn't need to assimilate to whiteness in order to be seen. The plot itself is wild and is honestly way too much to get into for a TikTok, but it was really creative and unlike anything I've ever seen before. I thought it was a little long and felt that some of the commentary and act 2 could be trimmed down because the implied commentary throughout act one stood for itself. But the show is currently in early preview, so I'm excited to see where it goes from here with that. Another playable for my collection.
